functions.name: llama_flash_attn_type_name

functions.description: Returns a human-readable name for a given llama_flash_attn_type value. Useful for logging or UI display.
requirements: flash_attn_type must be a valid value of enum llama_flash_attn_type.

functions.name: llama_model_default_params
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_model_params llama_model_default_params(void);
functions.description: Returns a struct with default initialization parameters for loading a model. Typical usage is to call this, then selectively override fields before passing into model load.

functions.name: llama_context_default_params
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_context_params llama_context_default_params(void);
functions.description: Returns default context parameters for initializing a llama_context. Callers usually modify fields (e.g., n_ctx, n_threads) then pass to llama_init_from_model.

functions.name: llama_sampler_chain_default_params
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler_chain_params llama_sampler_chain_default_params(void);
functions.description: Returns default parameters for creating a sampler chain. Modify returned fields if needed before calling llama_sampler_chain_init.

functions.name: llama_model_quantize_default_params
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_model_quantize_params llama_model_quantize_default_params(void);
functions.description: Returns default quantization parameters for llama_model_quantize.

functions.name: llama_backend_init
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_backend_init(void);
functions.description: Initializes the llama and ggml backend. Call once at program start before any other API usage.
requirements: Should be called once at the start of the program before using other llama APIs.

functions.name: llama_backend_free
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_backend_free(void);
functions.description: Finalizes backend resources. Call once at program exit. Currently used for MPI cleanup.
requirements: Should be called once at the end of the program.
Call after all contexts/models are freed.

functions.name: llama_numa_init
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_numa_init(enum ggml_numa_strategy numa);
functions.description: Optional initialization to configure NUMA strategy for the backend.
requirements: numa must be a valid enum ggml_numa_strategy.
Optional; call before creating contexts for effect.

functions.name: llama_attach_threadpool
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_attach_threadpool(struct llama_context * ctx, ggml_threadpool_t threadpool, ggml_threadpool_t threadpool_batch);
functions.description: Attaches explicit ggml threadpools to a llama_context, overriding the auto-created ones. Allows finer control of threading for generation and batch processing.
requirements: ctx must be a valid initialized llama_context.
threadpool and/or threadpool_batch should be valid ggml threadpool handles if provided.

functions.name: llama_detach_threadpool
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_detach_threadpool(struct llama_context * ctx);
functions.description: Detaches previously attached threadpools from a context, returning to default (auto) threadpool behavior.
requirements: ctx must be a valid initialized llama_context.

functions.name: llama_load_model_from_file
functions.signature: DEPRECATED(LLAMA_API struct llama_model * llama_load_model_from_file(const char * path_model, struct llama_model_params params), "use llama_model_load_from_file instead");
functions.description: DEPRECATED. Loads a model from a single GGUF file path with provided parameters. Use llama_model_load_from_file instead.
requirements: path_model must point to an accessible model file.
params should typically come from llama_model_default_params().

functions.name: llama_model_load_from_file
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_model * llama_model_load_from_file(const char * path_model, struct llama_model_params params);
functions.description: Loads a model from a file path. For split files, name must follow <name>-%05d-of-%05d.gguf unless using llama_model_load_from_splits.
requirements: path_model must reference a valid GGUF model file (or split series following the required naming).
params should be initialized (e.g., via llama_model_default_params).
If split model uses nonstandard names, use llama_model_load_from_splits instead.

functions.name: llama_model_load_from_splits
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_model * llama_model_load_from_splits(const char ** paths, size_t n_paths, struct llama_model_params params);
functions.description: Loads a model provided as multiple split files with custom naming. Paths must be provided in correct order.
requirements: paths must be a valid array of length n_paths containing readable split file paths in correct order.
params should be initialized (e.g., via llama_model_default_params).

functions.name: llama_model_save_to_file
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_model_save_to_file(const struct llama_model * model, const char * path_model);
functions.description: Saves the provided model to a file path in GGUF format.
requirements: model must be a valid loaded llama_model.
path_model must be a writable location.

functions.name: llama_free_model
functions.signature: DEPRECATED(LLAMA_API void llama_free_model(struct llama_model * model), "use llama_model_free instead");
functions.description: DEPRECATED. Frees a model instance. Use llama_model_free.
requirements: model must either be NULL or a valid model previously returned by a load function.

functions.name: llama_model_free
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_model_free(struct llama_model * model);
functions.description: Frees a model and its resources.
requirements: model must either be NULL or a valid model pointer obtained from load calls.
Do not use model after freeing.

functions.name: llama_init_from_model
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_context * llama_init_from_model(struct llama_model * model, struct llama_context_params params);
functions.description: Creates a llama_context from an already loaded model using the given context parameters.
requirements: model must be a valid loaded llama_model.
params should be initialized (e.g., via llama_context_default_params).

functions.name: llama_new_context_with_model
functions.signature: DEPRECATED(LLAMA_API struct llama_context * llama_new_context_with_model(struct llama_model * model, struct llama_context_params params), "use llama_init_from_model instead");
functions.description: DEPRECATED. Use llama_init_from_model. Creates a context from a model with provided parameters.

functions.name: llama_free
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_free(struct llama_context * ctx);
functions.description: Frees a llama_context and all its memory.
requirements: ctx must either be NULL or a valid context obtained from init.
Do not use ctx after freeing.

functions.name: llama_time_us

functions.name: llama_supports_mmap

functions.name: llama_supports_mlock

functions.name: llama_supports_gpu_offload

functions.name: llama_n_seq_max
functions.signature: LLAMA_API uint32_t llama_n_seq_max(const struct llama_context * ctx);
functions.description: Returns the actual maximum number of sequences supported by ctx.

functions.name: llama_n_ctx_train

functions.name: llama_n_layer
functions.signature: DEPRECATED(LLAMA_API int32_t llama_n_layer(const struct llama_model * model), "use llama_model_n_layer instead");
functions.description: DEPRECATED. Use llama_model_n_layer. Returns number of layers.

functions.name: llama_n_head
functions.signature: DEPRECATED(LLAMA_API int32_t llama_n_head(const struct llama_model * model), "use llama_model_n_head instead");

functions.signature: LLAMA_API bool llama_model_is_hybrid(const struct llama_model * model);

functions.name: llama_model_is_diffusion
functions.signature: LLAMA_API bool llama_model_is_diffusion(const struct llama_model * model);
functions.description: Returns true if the model is diffusion-based (e.g., LLaDA, Dream).

functions.name: llama_model_quantize
functions.signature: LLAMA_API uint32_t llama_model_quantize(const char * fname_inp, const char * fname_out, const llama_model_quantize_params * params);
functions.description: Quantizes a model file and writes the quantized result to an output file. Returns 0 on success.
requirements: fname_inp must be an existing readable model file.
fname_out must be a writable destination path.
params must point to a valid llama_model_quantize_params (initialize via llama_model_quantize_default_params).

functions.name: llama_adapter_lora_init
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_adapter_lora * llama_adapter_lora_init(struct llama_model * model, const char * path_lora);
functions.description: Loads a LoRA adapter from a file for the given model and returns a handle. The adapter is tied to the model and freed when the model is deleted.
requirements: model must be a valid model compatible with the adapter.
path_lora must be a readable LoRA GGUF file.

functions.name: llama_adapter_meta_val_str
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_adapter_meta_val_str(const struct llama_adapter_lora * adapter, const char * key, char * buf, size_t buf_size);
functions.description: Gets adapter’s GGUF metadata scalar value as a string by key. Returns length on success, -1 on failure. Output is null-terminated and cleared on failure.
requirements: key must be a metadata key name.
buf must be writable with capacity >= 1.

functions.name: llama_adapter_meta_count
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_adapter_meta_count(const struct llama_adapter_lora * adapter);
functions.description: Returns the number of metadata key/value pairs in the adapter.

functions.name: llama_adapter_meta_key_by_index
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_adapter_meta_key_by_index(const struct llama_adapter_lora * adapter, int32_t i, char * buf, size_t buf_size);
functions.description: Gets adapter metadata key name by index into buf. Returns length on success, -1 on failure. Output is null-terminated and cleared on failure.
requirements: i must be in range [0, llama_adapter_meta_count(adapter)).
buf must be a valid buffer with size > 0.

functions.name: llama_adapter_meta_val_str_by_index
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_adapter_meta_val_str_by_index(const struct llama_adapter_lora * adapter, int32_t i, char * buf, size_t buf_size);
functions.description: Gets adapter metadata value by index as string into buf. Returns length on success, -1 on failure. Output is null-terminated and cleared on failure.
requirements: i must be in range [0, llama_adapter_meta_count(adapter)).
buf must be a valid buffer with size > 0.

functions.name: llama_adapter_lora_free
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_adapter_lora_free(struct llama_adapter_lora * adapter);
functions.description: Frees a previously loaded LoRA adapter. Note: adapters are also freed when the associated model is deleted.
requirements: adapter must be either NULL or a valid adapter handle.

functions.name: llama_adapter_get_alora_n_invocation_tokens
functions.signature: LLAMA_API uint64_t llama_adapter_get_alora_n_invocation_tokens(const struct llama_adapter_lora * adapter);
functions.description: For alora adapters, returns the number of invocation tokens required. Otherwise, returns 0 or model-dependent value.

functions.name: llama_adapter_get_alora_invocation_tokens
functions.signature: LLAMA_API const llama_token * llama_adapter_get_alora_invocation_tokens(const struct llama_adapter_lora * adapter);
functions.description: For alora adapters, returns pointer to the invocation token array. Length given by llama_adapter_get_alora_n_invocation_tokens.

functions.name: llama_set_adapter_lora
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_set_adapter_lora(struct llama_context * ctx, struct llama_adapter_lora * adapter, float scale);
functions.description: Adds a loaded LoRA adapter to the given context with a specified scale. Does not modify model weights.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context associated with the model used to load adapter.
adapter must be a valid loaded adapter compatible with ctx’s model.
scale should be a finite float.

functions.name: llama_rm_adapter_lora
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_rm_adapter_lora(struct llama_context * ctx, struct llama_adapter_lora * adapter);
functions.description: Removes a specific LoRA adapter from the context. Returns -1 if not present.
requirements: adapter must be a valid adapter handle.

functions.name: llama_clear_adapter_lora
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_clear_adapter_lora(struct llama_context * ctx);
functions.description: Removes all LoRA adapters from the context.

functions.name: llama_apply_adapter_cvec
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_apply_adapter_cvec(struct llama_context * ctx, const float * data, size_t len, int32_t n_embd, int32_t il_start, int32_t il_end);
functions.description: Applies a control vector to a context, or clears the current one if data is NULL. The data should be a buffer for layers [il_start..il_end], each of length n_embd. See notes in header.
requirements: If data is not NULL: len must match n_embd * number_of_layers_in_range (implementation-defined).
il_start and il_end define an inclusive layer range within model bounds.
n_embd should match model’s embedding size for a single layer.

functions.name: llama_memory_clear
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_memory_clear(llama_memory_t mem, bool data);
functions.description: Clears memory contents (KV cache/state). If data is true, clears data buffers along with metadata.
requirements: mem must be a valid memory handle from llama_get_memory.
Use with caution during generation as it resets state.

functions.name: llama_memory_seq_rm
functions.signature: LLAMA_API bool llama_memory_seq_rm(llama_memory_t mem, llama_seq_id seq_id, llama_pos p0, llama_pos p1);
functions.description: Removes all tokens belonging to the sequence with positions in [p0, p1). Removing a whole sequence never fails; partial removals may fail (returns false).
requirements: Use p0 < 0 to mean [0, p1], and p1 < 0 to mean [p0, inf).

functions.name: llama_memory_seq_cp
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_memory_seq_cp(llama_memory_t mem, llama_seq_id seq_id_src, llama_seq_id seq_id_dst, llama_pos p0, llama_pos p1);
functions.description: Copies tokens from src sequence to dst sequence within position range [p0, p1).
requirements: Use p0 < 0 to mean [0, p1]; p1 < 0 to mean [p0, inf).
seq_id_src and seq_id_dst must refer to valid sequences or creation semantics are implementation-defined.

functions.name: llama_memory_seq_keep
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_memory_seq_keep(llama_memory_t mem, llama_seq_id seq_id);
functions.description: Removes all tokens not belonging to the specified sequence, keeping only that sequence.
requirements: seq_id must reference an existing sequence or semantics are implementation-defined.

functions.name: llama_memory_seq_add
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_memory_seq_add(llama_memory_t mem, llama_seq_id seq_id, llama_pos p0, llama_pos p1, llama_pos delta);
functions.description: Adds relative position delta to tokens of a sequence within [p0, p1). Useful for shifting positions.
requirements: Use p0/p1 < 0 for open intervals as documented.
delta must be an integer offset; ensure resulting positions remain in valid range for the model.

functions.name: llama_memory_seq_div
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_memory_seq_div(llama_memory_t mem, llama_seq_id seq_id, llama_pos p0, llama_pos p1, int d);
functions.description: Divides positions in [p0, p1) by factor d (>1).
requirements: Use p0/p1 < 0 for open intervals as documented.

functions.name: llama_memory_seq_pos_min
functions.signature: LLAMA_API llama_pos llama_memory_seq_pos_min(llama_memory_t mem, llama_seq_id seq_id);
functions.description: Returns smallest position present in memory for the sequence (useful with SWA). Returns -1 if empty.

functions.name: llama_memory_seq_pos_max
functions.signature: LLAMA_API llama_pos llama_memory_seq_pos_max(llama_memory_t mem, llama_seq_id seq_id);
functions.description: Returns largest position present in memory for the sequence. Returns -1 if empty.

functions.name: llama_memory_can_shift
functions.signature: LLAMA_API bool llama_memory_can_shift(llama_memory_t mem);
functions.description: Returns true if the memory supports shifting operations.

functions.name: llama_state_get_size
functions.signature: LLAMA_API size_t llama_state_get_size(struct llama_context * ctx);
functions.description: Returns the actual size in bytes of the complete state (logits, embeddings, memory). Use only when saving state.
requirements: Use only for saving; not for restoring (size may be too small otherwise).

functions.name: llama_get_state_size
functions.signature: LLAMA_API DEPRECATED(size_t llama_get_state_size(struct llama_context * ctx), "use llama_state_get_size instead");
functions.description: DEPRECATED. Use llama_state_get_size.

functions.name: llama_state_get_data
functions.signature: LLAMA_API size_t llama_state_get_data(struct llama_context * ctx, uint8_t * dst, size_t size);
functions.description: Copies the full state into dst up to size bytes. Returns number of bytes copied. Destination must be large enough (typically llama_state_get_size).
requirements: dst must point to a buffer of at least 'size' bytes.
Caller should have previously queried llama_state_get_size to allocate dst.

functions.name: llama_copy_state_data
functions.signature: LLAMA_API DEPRECATED(size_t llama_copy_state_data(struct llama_context * ctx, uint8_t * dst), "use llama_state_get_data instead");
functions.description: DEPRECATED. Use llama_state_get_data.
requirements: dst must be a sufficiently large buffer.

functions.name: llama_state_set_data
functions.signature: LLAMA_API size_t llama_state_set_data(struct llama_context * ctx, const uint8_t * src, size_t size);
functions.description: Restores state from src buffer. Returns number of bytes read.
requirements: ctx must be valid and compatible with the saved state.
src must point to a buffer containing a previously saved state.
size must be the size of the provided buffer.

functions.name: llama_set_state_data
functions.signature: LLAMA_API DEPRECATED(size_t llama_set_state_data(struct llama_context * ctx, const uint8_t * src), "use llama_state_set_data instead");
functions.description: DEPRECATED. Use llama_state_set_data.
requirements: src must point to a valid saved state buffer.

functions.name: llama_state_load_file
functions.signature: LLAMA_API bool llama_state_load_file(struct llama_context * ctx, const char * path_session, llama_token * tokens_out, size_t n_token_capacity, size_t * n_token_count_out);
functions.description: Loads a session/state from a file. Optionally outputs the stored tokens into provided buffer. Returns true on success.
requirements: path_session must be a readable session file path.
If tokens_out is non-NULL, it must have capacity n_token_capacity; n_token_count_out receives actual count.

functions.name: llama_load_session_file
functions.signature: LLAMA_API DEPRECATED(bool llama_load_session_file(struct llama_context * ctx, const char * path_session, llama_token * tokens_out, size_t n_token_capacity, size_t * n_token_count_out), "use llama_state_load_file instead");
functions.description: DEPRECATED. Use llama_state_load_file.

functions.name: llama_state_save_file
functions.signature: LLAMA_API bool llama_state_save_file(struct llama_context * ctx, const char * path_session, const llama_token * tokens, size_t n_token_count);
functions.description: Saves the current session/state to a file and optionally stores the provided tokens. Returns true on success.
requirements: path_session must be a writable file path.
If tokens is non-NULL, it must point to at least n_token_count tokens.

functions.name: llama_save_session_file
functions.signature: LLAMA_API DEPRECATED(bool llama_save_session_file(struct llama_context * ctx, const char * path_session, const llama_token * tokens, size_t n_token_count), "use llama_state_save_file instead");
functions.description: DEPRECATED. Use llama_state_save_file.

functions.name: llama_state_seq_get_size
functions.signature: LLAMA_API size_t llama_state_seq_get_size(struct llama_context * ctx, llama_seq_id seq_id);
functions.description: Returns the exact size needed to copy the state of a single sequence.
requirements: seq_id must refer to an existing sequence in ctx.

functions.name: llama_state_seq_get_data
functions.signature: LLAMA_API size_t llama_state_seq_get_data(struct llama_context * ctx, uint8_t * dst, size_t size, llama_seq_id seq_id);
functions.description: Copies the state of a single sequence into dst up to size bytes. Returns bytes written.
requirements: dst must be a buffer of at least 'size' bytes.
seq_id must refer to an existing sequence.

functions.name: llama_state_seq_set_data
functions.signature: LLAMA_API size_t llama_state_seq_set_data(struct llama_context * ctx, const uint8_t * src, size_t size, llama_seq_id dest_seq_id);
functions.description: Loads previously saved sequence state data into dest_seq_id. Returns positive on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: src must contain a sequence state buffer created by llama_state_seq_get_data.
dest_seq_id must be a valid sequence id in ctx.

functions.name: llama_state_seq_save_file
functions.signature: LLAMA_API size_t llama_state_seq_save_file(struct llama_context * ctx, const char * filepath, llama_seq_id seq_id, const llama_token * tokens, size_t n_token_count);
functions.description: Saves a single sequence’s state to a file, along with optional tokens. Returns bytes written or 0 on failure.
requirements: If tokens is non-NULL, it must point to at least n_token_count tokens.

functions.name: llama_state_seq_load_file
functions.signature: LLAMA_API size_t llama_state_seq_load_file(struct llama_context * ctx, const char * filepath, llama_seq_id dest_seq_id, llama_token * tokens_out, size_t n_token_capacity, size_t * n_token_count_out);
functions.description: Loads a single sequence’s state from a file into dest_seq_id and optionally returns tokens. Returns positive on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: filepath must be a readable file.
If tokens_out is non-NULL, it must have capacity n_token_capacity; n_token_count_out receives actual count.

functions.name: llama_state_seq_get_size_ext
functions.signature: LLAMA_API size_t llama_state_seq_get_size_ext(struct llama_context * ctx, llama_seq_id seq_id, llama_state_seq_flags flags);
functions.description: Extended version of sequence state size query, restricted to partial states depending on flags (e.g., SWA-only or partial-only).
requirements: seq_id must refer to an existing sequence.
flags should be a combination of llama_state_seq_flags; only partial states may be supported depending on flags.

functions.name: llama_state_seq_get_data_ext
functions.signature: LLAMA_API size_t llama_state_seq_get_data_ext(struct llama_context * ctx, uint8_t * dst, size_t size, llama_seq_id seq_id, llama_state_seq_flags flags);
functions.description: Extended sequence state export honoring flags (e.g., partial-only). Writes up to size bytes into dst and returns bytes written.
requirements: dst must be a buffer of at least 'size' bytes.
seq_id must refer to an existing sequence.
flags must be compatible with the sequence/state being exported.

functions.name: llama_state_seq_set_data_ext
functions.signature: LLAMA_API size_t llama_state_seq_set_data_ext(struct llama_context * ctx, const uint8_t * src, size_t size, llama_seq_id dest_seq_id, llama_state_seq_flags flags);
functions.description: Extended sequence state import honoring flags. Returns positive on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: src must contain a compatible sequence state buffer exported with matching flags.
dest_seq_id must be valid in ctx.
flags must match the exported data.

functions.name: llama_batch_get_one
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_batch llama_batch_get_one(llama_token * tokens, int32_t n_tokens);
functions.description: Helper to create a llama_batch for a single sequence of tokens with seq_id=0 and automatic position tracking by llama_decode. Intended for transition to new batch API.
requirements: tokens must point to at least n_tokens llama_token values.
This helper should be avoided for new code; prefer building llama_batch explicitly.

functions.name: llama_batch_init
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_batch llama_batch_init(int32_t n_tokens, int32_t embd, int32_t n_seq_max);
functions.description: Allocates a batch capable of holding up to n_tokens. If embd != 0, allocates space for embeddings, otherwise for tokens. Must be freed with llama_batch_free. Arrays left uninitialized.
requirements: Caller must initialize fields before use where required.
Must call llama_batch_free to release resources.

functions.name: llama_batch_free
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_batch_free(struct llama_batch batch);
functions.description: Frees memory allocated by llama_batch_init.
requirements: batch must be previously returned by llama_batch_init.

functions.name: llama_encode
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_encode(struct llama_context * ctx, struct llama_batch batch);
functions.description: Processes a batch via the encoder (no KV cache). For encoder-decoder models, stores encoder output internally for decoder cross-attention. Returns 0 on success, <0 on error; memory state is restored on error.
requirements: batch must be correctly populated; token or embd arrays sized to n_tokens; pos/seq arrays sized if provided.

functions.name: llama_decode
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_decode(struct llama_context * ctx, struct llama_batch batch);
functions.description: Processes a batch via the decoder. Requires context to have a memory. Return codes: 0 success; 1 no KV slot; 2 aborted (processed ubatches remain in memory); -1 invalid batch; < -1 fatal (processed ubatches remain). On other returns, memory state is restored.
requirements: ctx must be valid and have an allocated memory/KV cache.
batch must be valid and consistent (arrays sized to n_tokens).
Caller should handle nonzero return codes per documentation, possibly inspecting memory via llama_memory_seq_pos_min/max.

functions.name: llama_set_n_threads
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_set_n_threads(struct llama_context * ctx, int32_t n_threads, int32_t n_threads_batch);
functions.description: Sets number of threads for single-token generation (n_threads) and for prompt/batch processing (n_threads_batch).
requirements: n_threads and n_threads_batch should be positive integers.

functions.name: llama_n_threads
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_n_threads(struct llama_context * ctx);
functions.description: Gets number of threads used for generation of a single token.

functions.name: llama_n_threads_batch
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_n_threads_batch(struct llama_context * ctx);
functions.description: Gets number of threads used for prompt/batch processing.

functions.name: llama_set_embeddings
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_set_embeddings(struct llama_context * ctx, bool embeddings);
functions.description: Enables or disables embeddings output from the context. Affects whether embeddings are produced alongside logits.

functions.name: llama_set_causal_attn
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_set_causal_attn(struct llama_context * ctx, bool causal_attn);
functions.description: Sets whether to use causal attention (attend only to past tokens).

functions.name: llama_set_warmup
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_set_warmup(struct llama_context * ctx, bool warmup);
functions.description: Enables warmup mode. If true, llama_decode activates all tensors to load/cache their weights.

functions.name: llama_set_abort_callback
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_set_abort_callback(struct llama_context * ctx, ggml_abort_callback abort_callback, void * abort_callback_data);
functions.description: Sets abort callback used to abort llama_decode() execution when it returns true. Currently works only with CPU execution.
requirements: abort_callback may be NULL to clear; data passed back as abort_callback_data.

functions.name: llama_synchronize
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_synchronize(struct llama_context * ctx);
functions.description: Blocks until all pending computations in the context are finished. Often unnecessary because getters synchronize implicitly.

functions.name: llama_get_logits
functions.signature: LLAMA_API float * llama_get_logits(struct llama_context * ctx);
functions.description: Returns pointer to contiguous logits buffer for outputs selected by batch.logits flags. Rows = number of outputs, Cols = n_vocab. Deprecated in favor of llama_get_logits_ith.
requirements: Only valid after a successful llama_decode producing logits.

functions.name: llama_get_logits_ith
functions.signature: LLAMA_API float * llama_get_logits_ith(struct llama_context * ctx, int32_t i);
functions.description: Returns pointer to logits array for the i-th output (or reversed index if i < 0). Returns NULL for invalid ids.
requirements: i must index an available output from the last llama_decode().

functions.name: llama_get_embeddings
functions.signature: LLAMA_API float * llama_get_embeddings(struct llama_context * ctx);
functions.description: Returns pointer to contiguous embeddings buffer for outputs selected by batch.logits flags when pooling_type is NONE or using a generative model. Otherwise returns NULL. Deprecated in favor of llama_get_embeddings_ith.
requirements: Only valid after a successful call producing embeddings and when pooling_type == NONE or using a generative model.

functions.name: llama_get_embeddings_ith
functions.signature: LLAMA_API float * llama_get_embeddings_ith(struct llama_context * ctx, int32_t i);
functions.description: Returns pointer to the embedding vector for the i-th output (or reversed index if i < 0). Shape [n_embd]. Returns NULL for invalid ids.
requirements: i must index an available output from the last encode/decode that produced embeddings.

functions.name: llama_get_embeddings_seq
functions.signature: LLAMA_API float * llama_get_embeddings_seq(struct llama_context * ctx, llama_seq_id seq_id);
functions.description: Returns the embedding for a sequence id. When pooling_type == RANK returns float[n_cls_out] of ranks; otherwise returns float[n_embd]. Returns NULL if pooling_type is NONE.

functions.name: llama_vocab_get_text
functions.signature: LLAMA_API const char * llama_vocab_get_text(const struct llama_vocab * vocab, llama_token token);
functions.description: Returns the text piece associated with a token id.
requirements: token must be in range [0, llama_vocab_n_tokens(vocab)) or valid special token.

functions.name: llama_vocab_get_score
functions.signature: LLAMA_API float llama_vocab_get_score(const struct llama_vocab * vocab, llama_token token);
functions.description: Returns the score associated with a token (as stored in vocab).

functions.name: llama_vocab_get_attr
functions.signature: LLAMA_API enum llama_token_attr llama_vocab_get_attr(const struct llama_vocab * vocab, llama_token token);
functions.description: Returns token attributes bitmask (unknown/unused/normal/control/etc.).

functions.name: llama_vocab_is_eog

functions.description: Returns true if the token is an end-of-generation token (e.g., EOS/EOT).

functions.name: llama_vocab_is_control
functions.signature: LLAMA_API bool llama_vocab_is_control(const struct llama_vocab * vocab, llama_token token);
functions.description: Returns true if the token is a control token (non-renderable).

functions.name: llama_vocab_bos
functions.signature: LLAMA_API llama_token llama_vocab_bos(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns beginning-of-sentence token id.

functions.name: llama_vocab_eos
functions.signature: LLAMA_API llama_token llama_vocab_eos(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns end-of-sentence token id.

functions.name: llama_vocab_eot
functions.signature: LLAMA_API llama_token llama_vocab_eot(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns end-of-turn token id.

functions.name: llama_vocab_sep
functions.signature: LLAMA_API llama_token llama_vocab_sep(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns separator token id.

functions.name: llama_vocab_nl
functions.signature: LLAMA_API llama_token llama_vocab_nl(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns newline token id.

functions.name: llama_vocab_pad
functions.signature: LLAMA_API llama_token llama_vocab_pad(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns padding token id.

functions.name: llama_vocab_mask
functions.signature: LLAMA_API llama_token llama_vocab_mask(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns mask token id.

functions.name: llama_vocab_get_add_bos
functions.signature: LLAMA_API bool llama_vocab_get_add_bos(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns whether the tokenizer configuration adds a BOS token automatically.

functions.name: llama_vocab_get_add_eos
functions.signature: LLAMA_API bool llama_vocab_get_add_eos(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns whether the tokenizer configuration adds an EOS token automatically.

functions.name: llama_vocab_get_add_sep
functions.signature: LLAMA_API bool llama_vocab_get_add_sep(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns whether the tokenizer configuration adds a SEP token automatically.

functions.name: llama_vocab_fim_pre
functions.signature: LLAMA_API llama_token llama_vocab_fim_pre(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns FIM (fill-in-the-middle) prefix token.

functions.name: llama_vocab_fim_suf
functions.signature: LLAMA_API llama_token llama_vocab_fim_suf(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns FIM suffix token.

functions.name: llama_vocab_fim_mid
functions.signature: LLAMA_API llama_token llama_vocab_fim_mid(const struct llama_vocab * vocab);
functions.description: Returns FIM middle token.

functions.name: llama_vocab_fim_pad

functions.name: llama_tokenize
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_tokenize(const struct llama_vocab * vocab, const char * text, int32_t text_len, llama_token * tokens, int32_t n_tokens_max, bool add_special, bool parse_special);
functions.description: Tokenizes input text using the given vocab. Returns number of tokens on success (<= n_tokens_max), negative on failure (absolute value is needed size), INT32_MIN on overflow. add_special allows BOS/EOS insertion depending on model; parse_special allows tokenizing special/control tokens.
requirements: text must point to at least text_len bytes; not necessarily null-terminated.
tokens must point to an array with capacity n_tokens_max if non-NULL.
Handle negative return (needed size) and INT32_MIN overflow.

functions.name: llama_token_to_piece
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_token_to_piece(const struct llama_vocab * vocab, llama_token token, char * buf, int32_t length, int32_t lstrip, bool special);
functions.description: Renders a token id into bytes (piece) without null terminator. Returns number of bytes written. Can skip up to lstrip leading spaces. If special is true, renders special tokens verbatim.
requirements: buf must be a buffer of at least 'length' bytes; no null terminator is written.

functions.name: llama_detokenize
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_detokenize(const struct llama_vocab * vocab, const llama_token * tokens, int32_t n_tokens, char * text, int32_t text_len_max, bool remove_special, bool unparse_special);
functions.description: Converts tokens into text (inverse of tokenize). Returns number of bytes written on success (<= text_len_max) or negative needed size on failure. remove_special strips BOS/EOS if configured; unparse_special renders special tokens.
requirements: tokens must point to n_tokens entries.
Caller must handle negative return indicating required size.

functions.name: llama_chat_apply_template
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_chat_apply_template(const char * tmpl, const struct llama_chat_message * chat, size_t n_msg, bool add_ass, char * buf, int32_t length);
functions.description: Applies a chat template (or model default if tmpl == NULL) to a list of messages and writes the formatted prompt into buf. Returns total bytes of formatted prompt; if larger than buffer, reallocate and reapply. Only supports a predefined set of templates (no full Jinja parser).
requirements: chat must point to an array of n_msg llama_chat_message entries.
buf must point to a buffer of size 'length'.
At least one of tmpl or model’s default template must exist (tmpl may be NULL).
Callers should allocate about 2x total input characters as a heuristic.

functions.name: llama_chat_builtin_templates
functions.signature: LLAMA_API int32_t llama_chat_builtin_templates(const char ** output, size_t len);
functions.description: Writes pointers to built-in chat template names into output (up to len). Returns the number of templates available (may exceed len).
requirements: output must be a buffer of const char* with capacity len if non-NULL.

functions.name: llama_sampler_init
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler * llama_sampler_init(const struct llama_sampler_i * iface, llama_sampler_context_t ctx);
functions.description: Creates a sampler from a user-provided interface and optional context pointer.
requirements: iface must not be NULL and should provide at least 'apply'.
ctx is an opaque user pointer passed to iface callbacks.

functions.name: llama_sampler_name
functions.signature: LLAMA_API const char * llama_sampler_name(const struct llama_sampler * smpl);
functions.description: Returns the name of a sampler if provided by its interface; otherwise may return NULL.

functions.name: llama_sampler_accept
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_sampler_accept(struct llama_sampler * smpl, llama_token token);
functions.description: Notifies the sampler that a token has been accepted into the sequence. Used by samplers that track history.

functions.name: llama_sampler_apply
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_sampler_apply(struct llama_sampler * smpl, llama_token_data_array * cur_p);
functions.description: Applies the sampler to modify candidate token probabilities/logits in-place. Required to set selected index as needed by chain.
requirements: cur_p->data must point to at least cur_p->size entries.
cur_p->selected should be set by the sampler that selects tokens.

functions.name: llama_sampler_reset
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_sampler_reset(struct llama_sampler * smpl);
functions.description: Resets sampler internal state (e.g., history).

functions.name: llama_sampler_clone
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler * llama_sampler_clone(const struct llama_sampler * smpl);
functions.description: Creates a clone of a sampler if supported by its interface. Returns NULL if not supported and ctx is NULL.

functions.name: llama_sampler_free
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_sampler_free(struct llama_sampler * smpl);
functions.description: Frees a sampler. Do not free if the sampler has been added to a chain (ownership transferred).
requirements: smpl must be valid or NULL.
Do not free a sampler after adding to a chain; the chain frees it.

functions.name: llama_sampler_chain_init
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler * llama_sampler_chain_init(struct llama_sampler_chain_params params);
functions.description: Creates a sampler chain which can host multiple samplers applied sequentially.

functions.name: llama_sampler_chain_add
functions.signature: LLAMA_API void llama_sampler_chain_add(struct llama_sampler * chain, struct llama_sampler * smpl);
functions.description: Adds a sampler to the chain. The chain takes ownership and will free it when the chain is freed.
requirements: chain must be a sampler created by llama_sampler_chain_init.
smpl must be a valid sampler; ownership is transferred.

functions.name: llama_sampler_chain_get

requirements: chain must be a sampler chain.

functions.name: llama_sampler_init_dist
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler * llama_sampler_init_dist(uint32_t seed);

requirements: seed sets the RNG; can use LLAMA_DEFAULT_SEED to auto-pick in some contexts.

functions.name: llama_sampler_init_top_k
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler * llama_sampler_init_top_k(int32_t k);
functions.description: Creates a Top-K sampler. If k <= 0, it becomes a no-op sampler.

functions.name: llama_sampler_init_top_p
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler * llama_sampler_init_top_p(float p, size_t min_keep);
functions.description: Creates a nucleus (top-p) sampler keeping minimal min_keep tokens.

min_keep >= 1 recommended to avoid empty set.

functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler * llama_sampler_init_min_p(float p, size_t min_keep);

functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler * llama_sampler_init_temp(float t);
functions.description: Creates a temperature sampler modifying logits by l_i = l_i / t. For t <= 0, keeps max logit and sets others to -inf (argmax).

functions.name: llama_sampler_init_temp_ext
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler * llama_sampler_init_temp_ext(float t, float delta, float exponent);
functions.description: Creates a dynamic temperature sampler (entropy-based) with parameters controlling adaptation.

functions.name: llama_sampler_init_xtc

functions.description: Creates an XTC sampler as described in TGI web UI PR. Combines probability and temperature with randomness.
requirements: p and t should be positive.

functions.name: llama_sampler_init_top_n_sigma
functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler * llama_sampler_init_top_n_sigma(float n);

functions.signature: LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler * llama_sampler_init_mirostat(int32_t n_vocab, uint32_t seed, float tau, float eta, int32_t m);
functions.description: Creates a Mirostat 1.0 sampler using token-level formulation. Controls target surprise (tau), learning rate (eta), and window m. Requires n_vocab.
requirements: n_vocab must be the model vocabulary size.
tau and eta should be positive.
m should be a positive integer.

functions.description: Initializes a GBNF grammar sampler. Returns empty grammar if grammar_str is empty, or NULL if parsing fails.
requirements: grammar_str may be empty; if not, it must contain valid GBNF rules.
grammar_root must name the start symbol within grammar_str.

functions.signature: DEPRECATED(LLAMA_API struct llama_sampler * llama_sampler_init_grammar_lazy(const struct llama_vocab * vocab, const char * grammar_str, const char * grammar_root, const char ** trigger_words, size_t num_trigger_words, const llama_token * trigger_tokens, size_t num_trigger_tokens), "use llama_sampler_init_grammar_lazy_patterns instead");

import io
import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# This generator produces a minimal, self-consistent GGUF v3/v2-like file that llama.cpp
# can parse as a vocab-only model. It includes:
# - GGUF header (magic, version, tensor/kv counts, alignment)
# - A few required GGUF metadata keys used by llama.cpp during model load
# - Zero tensors (compatible with vocab_only and lightweight loading)
# - Properly encoded string/array values using GGUF type tags
#
# Notes:
# - We avoid any external deps and keep file under 4 KiB.
# - We target a very small vocab and minimal hyperparameters.
# - Even if llama.cpp evolves, these keys are broadly recognized and harmless.

# GGUF constants (from public format docs / llama.cpp conventions)
MAGIC = b"GGUF"
# Choose a commonly supported version: 3
GGUF_VERSION = 3
ALIGNMENT = 32  # standard alignment used by llama.cpp

# GGUF type enum (subset used here). These values match gguf_type in llama.cpp
GGUF_TYPE_UINT8   = 0
GGUF_TYPE_INT8    = 1
GGUF_TYPE_UINT16  = 2
GGUF_TYPE_INT16   = 3
GGUF_TYPE_UINT32  = 4
GGUF_TYPE_INT32   = 5
GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT32 = 6
GGUF_TYPE_BOOL    = 7
GGUF_TYPE_STRING  = 8
GGUF_TYPE_ARRAY   = 9
GGUF_TYPE_UINT64  = 10
GGUF_TYPE_INT64   = 11
GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT64 = 12

# Helper: write a length-prefixed UTF-8 string as used by GGUF (u64 length + bytes)
def _enc_str(s: str) -> bytes:
    b = s.encode('utf-8')
    return struct.pack('<Q', len(b)) + b

# Helper: encode a GGUF scalar value with its type tag
def _enc_scalar(typ: int, val) -> bytes:
    if typ == GGUF_TYPE_BOOL:
        return struct.pack('<B', 1 if val else 0)
    if typ == GGUF_TYPE_UINT8:
        return struct.pack('<B', val & 0xFF)
    if typ == GGUF_TYPE_INT8:
        return struct.pack('<b', int(val))
    if typ == GGUF_TYPE_UINT16:
        return struct.pack('<H', val & 0xFFFF)
    if typ == GGUF_TYPE_INT16:
        return struct.pack('<h', int(val))
    if typ == GGUF_TYPE_UINT32:
        return struct.pack('<I', val & 0xFFFFFFFF)
    if typ == GGUF_TYPE_INT32:
        return struct.pack('<i', int(val))
    if typ == GGUF_TYPE_UINT64:
        return struct.pack('<Q', int(val) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)
    if typ == GGUF_TYPE_INT64:
        return struct.pack('<q', int(val))
    if typ == GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT32:
        return struct.pack('<f', float(val))
    if typ == GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT64:
        return struct.pack('<d', float(val))
    if typ == GGUF_TYPE_STRING:
        return _enc_str(str(val))
    raise ValueError('unsupported scalar type')

# Helper: encode a GGUF array header and its elements
# Array layout: u32 elem_type, u64 n, then n elements encoded as scalars (without per-element type tags)
def _enc_array(elem_type: int, values: List) -> bytes:
    out = io.BytesIO()
    out.write(struct.pack('<I', elem_type))
    out.write(struct.pack('<Q', len(values)))
    for v in values:
        if elem_type == GGUF_TYPE_STRING:
            out.write(_enc_str(str(v)))
        else:
            out.write(_enc_scalar(elem_type, v))
    return out.getvalue()

# Helper: write a GGUF key-value entry: key string, value type tag, then payload
# Key is encoded as length-prefixed string
# Value: u32 type, then data as per type

def _enc_kv(key: str, vtype: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    return _enc_str(key) + struct.pack('<I', vtype) + payload

# Build a minimal set of metadata keys. These are common in llama.cpp and help it recognize the file.
# We randomize some innocuous values based on seed to create diversity while remaining valid.

def _build_metadata(rng: random.Random) -> List[Tuple[str, int, bytes]]:
    # required-like keys for llama models
    # general
    architecture = rng.choice(["llama", "mamba", "rwkv", "granite"])  # llama.cpp accepts various; "llama" safest
    vocab_size = rng.choice([128, 256, 512, 1024])  # tiny for vocab_only use
    n_layer = rng.choice([2, 4, 6])
    n_head = rng.choice([2, 4, 8])
    n_head_kv = rng.choice([1, 2, 4])
    n_embd = rng.choice([64, 128, 256])
    n_ctx_train = rng.choice([256, 512, 1024])
    rope_scaling = "none"
    file_type = 1  # Mostly F16 (common); used by some tooling though tensors are zero here

    # tokenizer block — minimal plausible values
    tokenizer_model = rng.choice(["spm", "bpe", "wpm"])  # map to llama_vocab_type
    tokenizer_pre = rng.choice(["llama", "llama2", "llama3"])  # descriptive only

    keys = []

    # core ident
    keys.append(("general.architecture", GGUF_TYPE_STRING, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_STRING, architecture)))
    keys.append(("general.name", GGUF_TYPE_STRING, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_STRING, "mini-gguf-vocab-only")))

    # model dimensions
    keys.append(("llama.context_length", GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, n_ctx_train)))
    keys.append(("llama.embedding_length", GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, n_embd)))
    keys.append(("llama.block_count", GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, n_layer)))
    keys.append(("llama.attention.head_count", GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, n_head)))
    keys.append(("llama.attention.head_count_kv", GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, n_head_kv)))
    keys.append(("llama.rope.dimension_count", GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, n_embd)))
    keys.append(("llama.rope.freq_base", GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_FLOAT32, 10000.0)))
    keys.append(("llama.rope.scaling.type", GGUF_TYPE_STRING, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_STRING, rope_scaling)))

    # vocab/tokenizer
    keys.append(("tokenizer.ggml.model", GGUF_TYPE_STRING, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_STRING, tokenizer_model)))
    keys.append(("tokenizer.ggml.pre", GGUF_TYPE_STRING, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_STRING, tokenizer_pre)))
    keys.append(("tokenizer.ggml.add_bos", GGUF_TYPE_BOOL, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_BOOL, True)))
    keys.append(("tokenizer.ggml.add_eos", GGUF_TYPE_BOOL, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_BOOL, False)))

    # vocab size and some dummy scores to satisfy readers that expect arrays to exist
    keys.append(("tokenizer.ggml.vocab_size", GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, vocab_size)))

    # Basic special tokens
    special_tokens = ["<|begin|>", "<|end|>", "<|pad|>", "<unk>"]
    keys.append(("tokenizer.ggml.bos_token_id", GGUF_TYPE_INT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_INT32, 0)))
    keys.append(("tokenizer.ggml.eos_token_id", GGUF_TYPE_INT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_INT32, 1)))
    keys.append(("tokenizer.ggml.pad_token_id", GGUF_TYPE_INT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_INT32, 2)))
    keys.append(("tokenizer.ggml.unknown_token_id", GGUF_TYPE_INT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_INT32, 3)))
    keys.append(("tokenizer.ggml.special.tokens", GGUF_TYPE_ARRAY, _enc_array(GGUF_TYPE_STRING, special_tokens)))

    # Optional descriptive fields
    keys.append(("general.quantization_version", GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, 0)))
    keys.append(("general.file_type", GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, _enc_scalar(GGUF_TYPE_UINT32, file_type)))

    return keys

# Assemble GGUF file

def _build_gguf(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    kv_entries = _build_metadata(rng)
    n_kv = len(kv_entries)
    n_tensors = 0  # vocab_only, no tensors

    # Header
    out = io.BytesIO()
    out.write(MAGIC)
    out.write(struct.pack('<I', GGUF_VERSION))
    out.write(struct.pack('<Q', n_tensors))
    out.write(struct.pack('<Q', n_kv))
    out.write(struct.pack('<Q', ALIGNMENT))

    # Placeholder for tensor infos (none)

    # Key-Value section
    for key, vtype, payload in kv_entries:
        out.write(_enc_kv(key, vtype, payload))

    # Alignment padding before tensor data (even if no tensors, many readers tolerate exact end)
    def pad_to(align: int):
        cur = out.tell()
        rem = (-cur) % align
        if rem:
            out.write(b"\0" * rem)

    pad_to(ALIGNMENT)

    # No tensor data

    data = out.getvalue()
    # Keep file within budget
    if len(data) > 4096:
        # Should not happen, but truncate extras if any padding pushed it over
        data = data[:4096]
    return data


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    # Produce a minimal, valid GGUF bytes buffer (vocab-only style) that loaders can parse.
    # The fuzz harness will write this to a temp file and pass the filename to llama_model_load_* APIs.
    return _build_gguf(seed)

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path
# Used by fuzzer stubs via FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() and FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for prefixes.
# We generate syntactically valid, writable-looking paths and filename prefixes that
# exercise split naming logic and various directory structures. No actual I/O occurs here;
# the fuzzer harness will create files if needed. We focus on plausible, valid paths.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."

def _rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, allow_ext: bool = True) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    base = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(max(1, n))).strip()
    # Ensure non-empty and not just spaces/dots
    if not base or all(c == '.' for c in base):
        base = 'file'
    # Randomly add extension(s)
    if allow_ext and rng.random() < 0.8:
        exts = ["gguf", "bin", "dat", "log", "txt", "session"]
        # Sometimes double extension
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            base += "." + rng.choice(exts) + "." + rng.choice(exts)
        else:
            base += "." + rng.choice(exts)
    return base

def _rand_dirs(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    depth = rng.randint(0, 4)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        # include some interesting directory names
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.15:
            parts.append(".")
        elif choice < 0.30:
            parts.append("..")
        else:
            parts.append(_rand_name(rng, 1, 8, allow_ext=False).replace(' ', '_'))
    return parts

def _split_prefix_variants(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate prefixes likely used with llama_split_path: <prefix>-00001-of-00004.gguf
    # Provide both plain prefix and one that already ends with dash or partial pattern
    base = _rand_name(rng, 3, 10, allow_ext=False).replace(' ', '_')
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return base
    # Sometimes include model-ish basename
    model_names = ["model", "llama", "mixtral", "qwen", "gemma", "rwkv", "granite"]
    prefix = rng.choice(model_names) + "-" + base
    # Occasionally end with a dash to test joining
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        prefix += "-"
    return prefix

def _platformize_path(rng: random.Random, parts: List[str], filename: str) -> str:
    # Mix separators to exercise path handling; prefer OS-native but keep validity
    sep = os.sep
    if os.name == 'nt':
        # create Windows-like paths sometimes
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            drive = rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase)
            prefix = f"{drive}:\\"
            joiner = "\\"
        else:
            prefix = "\\\\?\\C:\\" if rng.random() < 0.3 else "\\\\.\\C:\\"
            joiner = "\\"
        path = prefix + joiner.join(parts + [filename]) if parts else prefix + filename
        return path
    else:
        # POSIX-like
        root = "/" if rng.random() < 0.8 else ""
        joiner = "/"
        path = root + joiner.join(parts + [filename]) if parts else root + filename
        return path

def _gen_filename_for_write(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose a filename targeted for write/save operations
    # Prefer .gguf or .session to align with API expectations
    base = _rand_name(rng, 3, 12, allow_ext=False).replace(' ', '_')
    ext = rng.choice(["gguf", "session", "state", "bin", "dat"]) if rng.random() < 0.9 else _rand_name(rng, 2, 4, allow_ext=False)
    fname = f"{base}.{ext}"
    # Sometimes include split suffix already, to test overwrite or detect naming
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        count = rng.randint(1, 64)
        no = rng.randint(1, count)
        fname = f"{base}-{no:05d}-of-{count:05d}.gguf"
    return fname

def _gen_interesting_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # 50%: path for writing model/state
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts = _rand_dirs(rng)
        fname = _gen_filename_for_write(rng)
        return _platformize_path(rng, parts, fname)
    # 30%: directory path that ends with a separator + base filename
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        parts = _rand_dirs(rng)
        # ensure at least one directory
        if not parts:
            parts = ["tmp"]
        fname = _rand_name(rng, 4, 10, allow_ext=True)
        return _platformize_path(rng, parts, fname)
    # 20%: split prefix like used by llama_split_path
    parts = _rand_dirs(rng)
    fname = _split_prefix_variants(rng)
    return _platformize_path(rng, parts, fname)

def _encode_bytes(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode to UTF-8, ensure max length
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > 4000:
        b = b[:4000]
    return b

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Create multiple candidates and pick one by RNG to provide variability per call
    candidates = []
    for _ in range(5):
        path = _gen_interesting_path(rng)
        candidates.append(path)
    # Additionally include a canonical split prefix string useful for llama_split_path
    prefix = _split_prefix_variants(rng)
    if os.name != 'nt':
        candidates.append(prefix)
    else:
        # On Windows, include prefix within a path to keep it valid
        candidates.append(_platformize_path(rng, ["CACHED", "MODELS"], prefix))

    choice = rng.choice(candidates)
    return _encode_bytes(choice)
